newsitem.title: GUYANA: Caribbean leaders pay tribute to Guyana's Jagan.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean leaders pay tribute to Guyana's Jagan.

text.p: Caribbean leaders gathered in Guyana's capital on Monday to pay their last respects to former President Cheddi Jagan, one of the leading figures of Caribbean Cold War politics.

P. J. Patterson and Basdeo Panday, the prime ministers of Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago, were among the regional dignitaries at a funeral ceremony held in the open courtyard of Parliament for Jagan, who died last Thursday.
Jagan's coffin, draped in the national flag, lay under a canopy as family members, religious and political leaders paid tribute to a man whose political career spanned five decades.
"Dr Jagan's spirit will continue...Our nation shall go forward stronger in unity," said former Prime Minister and now interim President Samuel Hinds.
Hinds was sworn in immediately after Jagan died from heart failure at Walter Reed hospital in Washington.

The most emotional words came from Jagan's son, Cheddi Jagan Jr., who addressed his father directly. "I will never forget the essence of yourself or the things that you stood for: the poor and the oppressed," he said.
Outside the parliament building tens of thousands of people jammed the streets in the largest show of mourning in the former British colony's history.
Jagan, a former Marxist, returned to power in Guyana in 1992 when he won the country's first democratic elections in 28 years.
In a letter to Hinds, Cuba's President Fidel Castro said Havana had lost a "great friend" and the Caribbean an "outstanding leader."
U.S. President Bill Clinton last week called Jagan "a champion of the poor".
The author of numerous books on Caribbean history, Jagan was Guyana's first prime minister when the Britain granted it self-government in 1961, only to be deposed three years later after race riots.
Among his works was "The Role of the CIA in Guyana and its Activities Throughout the World," published in 1967, which did not endear him to Washington.
Jagan was to be cremated on Tuesday at his birthplace Port Mourant, 90 miles (145 km) east of Georgetown.
